title: When the Alibi Wakes
premise: Ivo Winterbourne, a night-shift dispatcher with a gift for reconstructing timelines, is handed a cold case: Marisol Quade vanished eleven years ago, and the statute expires in thirty days. When Ivo tracks down Marisol's diary and finds entries written after the disappearance date, she realizes someone has been keeping the diary alive—either the missing woman or her killer. As Ivo follows the diary's coded routes through the city's taxi grid, she uncovers that Marisol faked her death to escape an inheritance scheme run by the family who took Ivo in as a foster teen. In the climax, Ivo baits the killer—the family patriarch's lawyer—into confessing on dispatch recordings, then reunites with Marisol, choosing found family over blood.
about_author: Wren Vane spent a decade answering late-night phones for a metropolitan cab company before turning those voices into fiction. They write mysteries about people the city overlooks, from a basement apartment lit by radio static.

chapters.title: The Last Fare
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A slow night at Dispatch ends when Detective Okafor drops a cold file on her desk: Marisol Quade, missing eleven years, statute expiring in a month. Ivo takes it out of pride, not pity. Emotional beat: the thrill of a puzzle meeting the dread of a deadline.

chapters.title: Diary of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She visits Marisol's abandoned storage unit and finds the diary—entries continuing three weeks past the disappearance date, in handwriting that matches samples perfectly. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case just stopped being paperwork and became impossible.

chapters.title: Handwriting on the Wall
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A forensic document examiner confirms the post-disappearance pages are authentic but written under duress—letters wobbling, phrases repeating like dictated code. Emotional beat: cold fear hardening into resolve; someone alive wrote these words.

chapters.title: The Winterbourne House
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The diary's coded addresses trace back to the Aldercrest estate of the Voss family—the same people who fostered Ivo at fifteen. Emotional beat: betrayal's first sting; every warm memory now reads like a cover story.

chapters.title: Gridlock
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, intercut with diary excerpts. The codes map to taxi routes Ivo knows by heart; Marisol was leaving breadcrumbs along the city's veins. Emotional beat: eerie intimacy—Ivo is reading a stranger's map of her own life.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Detective Okafor's POV. He warns Ivo off: the original investigator on the Quade case died suspiciously, and the file has been touched by someone inside. Emotional beat: protective friction; two stubborn people circling the same truth.

chapters.title: The Lawyer Who Never Sleeps
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She surveils Corwin Ashe, the Voss family attorney who handled Marisol's contested inheritance—and notices his car following the exact coded routes. Emotional beat: hunter's patience sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Someone wipes the dispatch archives from the week Marisol vanished; only Ivo's private logbooks survive. Emotional beat: violation and vindication—they're erasing evidence because she's close.

chapters.title: Aldercrest After Dark
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At a Voss dinner party, Ivo plays the grateful ward while pocketing a key to Ashe's study. Emotional beat: double life tightening; every smile costs her something.

chapters.title: The Study
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Inside Ashe's study she finds Marisol's original will, altered after her death, and a second diary—blank pages pre-dated years in advance. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing; the inheritance scheme was rehearsed like theater.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Dredging records surface a witness: a tow-truck driver who saw Marisol alive at the river dock weeks after her 'death.' Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as more danger.

chapters.title: The Dock at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the final diary entry to the dock, Ivo is ambushed by an unknown watcher who leaves her alive with a warning: stop reading. Emotional beat: terror braided with proof—Marisol may still be breathing.

chapters.title: Blood and Ink
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Comparing both diaries, Ivo cracks the cipher: the post-disappearance entries are Marisol's hostage letters, dictating terms Ashe never intended to honor. Emotional beat: grief for a woman writing to be found.

chapters.title: The Ward's Privilege
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Old Mrs. Voss, lucid for one afternoon, tells Ivo that Marisol discovered the family fortune was built on forged deeds—and that they 'handled' anyone who looked too long. Emotional beat: orphaned twice over; the found family was the trap.

chapters.title: Deadline Math
chapters.summary: Ivo and Okafor's alternating POV. With nine days left, they plan to make Ashe confess before the statute kills the case forever. Emotional beat: grim camaraderie; the clock becomes their ally.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She leaks word that the surviving diary will be handed to prosecutors, forcing Ashe to move against her. Emotional beat: calculated recklessness; she is finally the one setting the route.

chapters.title: Dispatch, Line One
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ashe calls the dispatch line to bargain, unaware every call is recorded; Ivo keeps him talking through the coded streets until he admits where Marisol was held. Emotional beat: white-knuckle triumph mid-sentence.

chapters.title: The Room Above the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Police raid the Voss boathouse and find evidence of eleven years of captivity—and signs Marisol escaped recently, alive. Emotional beat: breathless release collapsing into urgency.

chapters.title: Ashe Runs
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ashe flees toward the airport using the very taxi routes from the diary; Ivo reroutes the night's cabs to box him in. Emotional beat: the dispatcher's quiet power turned into a net.

chapters.title: Confession at Kilometer Zero
chapters.summary: Climax. Ivo confronts Ashe at the old depot, recordings rolling, as he reveals Mrs. Voss ordered everything and Marisol's escape was bought with silence. Arrest comes; the statute question dies with his confession. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into justice.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Resolution. A letter arrives, postmarked the day after the arrest: Marisol, watching from afar, writes that she'll come home when it's safe. Ivo mails back a single reply: the case is closed, the door is open. Emotional beat: ache softening into patience.

chapters.title: When the Alibi Wakes
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ivo's POV. Months later, Marisol walks into Dispatch at 3 a.m.; the two women share coffee among the radios while Okafor closes the file for good. Ivo realizes family is whoever answers when you call. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and kept.
